ENTRY 001 · 2026-09-17 · KANSAS CITY

I got bored and finally made a website

REV A · 2 MIN READ

Eighty-nine repositories. Four hundred stars. Twenty-odd years of shipping Java that other people’s builds quietly depend on. And until today, the only thing on the internet with my name on it was a GitHub profile and a WordPress blog whose password I genuinely do not remember.

So: here is a website. I got bored, which is historically how all of my projects begin.

It looks like a shop drawing because that is how my head is organized. Parts, tolerances, revision history, a title block in the corner telling you who drew the thing and at what scale. I like engineering of every flavor — mechanical, civil, the kind with grease on it — and a blueprint is the most honest document in the world. It does not sell you anything. It just tells you exactly what the part is and how much slop is allowed.

Software could use more of that. Fewer landing pages, more datasheets.

What’s actually on here

Two things I care about most got real write-ups. petrify compiles ML models — ONNX, XGBoost, LightGBM, scikit-learn — straight into JVM bytecode, so inference is just comparisons and jumps instead of an interpreter dragging a 150MB native library around. locksmith is a Maven extension that pulls your secrets out of the macOS Keychain instead of a plaintext settings.xml that we all pretend is fine.

The rest of the repositories are pulled live off the GitHub API into a bill of materials, because maintaining a list by hand is how lists become lies.

What goes here next

Bytecode notes, mostly. How petrify lays a tree ensemble into the constant pool. Why the JDK 25 Class-File API made the whole compiler about a third the size it used to be. Maven extension internals, which are documented approximately nowhere. And occasionally a trail report, because I test my gear the hard way and the ivy around here holds a grudge.

No schedule. No newsletter. No cookie banner. Just notes, filed as I make them.
